Heritage walk in Mysuru: the palace, the markets and Srirangapatna

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Mysuru (Mysore) covers the Wodeyar capital rebuilt after 1799: Mysore Palace, finished in 1912, the Devaraja Market and the civic buildings around it. Most groups add Srirangapatna, Tipu Sultan's island capital 15 km away, and the Hoysala temple at Somanathapura, which needs a vehicle and about an hour by road.

We arrange Mysuru heritage walks on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, led by an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, with other languages through partners.

Why Mysuru matters for heritage

The Wodeyar kings of Mysore ruled from Mysuru from the late 14th century, moved their capital to Srirangapatna in 1610, and lost real power to Hyder Ali and his son Tipu Sultan in the 1760s. After Tipu's death in 1799 the British restored the Wodeyars and the capital returned to Mysuru. The present city, with its broad roads, circles, palaces and public buildings, is largely the work of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, when Mysore was known as a well-run princely state.

That makes Mysuru a good place to study how an Indian court used architecture to present itself as both traditional and modern. The Dasara procession, the palace durbar hall and the city plan all served that purpose.

Historical places in and around Mysuru by period

Some of the oldest evidence is outside the city. Somanathapura's Keshava Temple was built in 1268 under the Hoysalas, and inscriptions on Chamundi Hill and around Srirangapatna go back many centuries. Srirangapatna's Ranganathaswamy Temple has origins in the Ganga and Hoysala periods, with Vijayanagara additions.

Srirangapatna is the 18th century layer: Tipu Sultan's fort, the Jama Masjid of 1784, the Daria Daulat Bagh summer palace (1784) and the Gumbaz where Hyder Ali and Tipu are buried. The 1799 siege ended Tipu's rule. Mysuru's own monuments are mainly later: the palace (1897 to 1912, by Henry Irwin), Jaganmohan Palace (1861), the Devaraja Market and Crawford Hall of the University of Mysore.

Places a heritage walk in Mysuru covers

  1. Mysore Palace 1897 to 1912

    Rebuilt after a fire, designed by Henry Irwin. See the Kalyana Mantapa and the Dasara procession paintings.

  2. Devaraja Market Late 19th century

    Arcaded market near the palace. A good place to talk about everyday trade and conservation of working buildings.

  3. Jaganmohan Palace 1861

    Used by the royal family while the main palace was rebuilt. Now an art gallery.

  4. Crawford Hall Early 20th century

    Administrative building of the University of Mysore, founded in 1916.

  5. St Philomena's Church 1936 to 1956

    Neo-Gothic church with tall twin spires, built with royal support.

  6. Chamundi Hill Temple tradition centuries old, gopuram 19th century

    The Chamundeshwari Temple and a 17th century monolithic Nandi on the steps. Reached by vehicle.

  7. Srirangapatna Fort 18th century

    Tipu Sultan's island fortress. Look for the breach point of 1799 and the dungeons.

  8. Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangapatna 9th century origins, later additions

    Vaishnava temple at the heart of the island town, older than the fort around it.

  9. Jama Masjid, Srirangapatna 1784

    Mosque built by Tipu Sultan with two tall minarets and Persian inscriptions.

  10. Daria Daulat Bagh 1784

    Tipu's summer palace in teak, with painted walls showing the Battle of Pollilur.

  11. Gumbaz 1784

    Mausoleum of Hyder Ali, his wife and Tipu Sultan, with lacquered doors inlaid with ivory.

  12. Keshava Temple, Somanathapura 1268

    Hoysala temple on a star-shaped plan, with three shrines and signed sculpture panels.

Walking routes in Mysuru

Palace and market on foot

About 3 hours

Mysore Palace → Devaraja Market → Jaganmohan Palace → Crawford Hall

Srirangapatna island

Half day, vehicle needed between clusters

Srirangapatna Fort → Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangapatna → Jama Masjid, Srirangapatna → Daria Daulat Bagh → Gumbaz

Somanathapura and Chamundi Hill

Half day by vehicle

Keshava Temple, Somanathapura → Chamundi Hill

Museums in Mysuru

  • Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery, Jaganmohan Palace. Raja Ravi Varma paintings, Mysore paintings and court objects.
  • Folklore Museum, University of Mysore. Folk objects, puppets and crafts in Jayalakshmi Vilas Mansion.
  • Daria Daulat Bagh Museum. Tipu Sultan's period objects and paintings at Srirangapatna.

Best time for a walk

October to February. Dasara (September or October) is spectacular but very crowded; plan school groups outside the festival week.

What you see on a heritage walk in Mysuru

Inside the palace, look at the Kalyana Mantapa with its stained glass ceiling and the paintings of the Dasara procession, which record the order of the parade around 1930. The architecture mixes Hindu, Mughal, Rajput and Gothic forms, the style historians call Indo-Saracenic. Outside the gates, the Devaraja Market sells flowers, betel leaves and kumkum in an arcaded building whose 19th century structure has been the subject of conservation debate.

At Srirangapatna the story is military and political. The Daria Daulat Bagh's painted walls show the Battle of Pollilur (1780), where Hyder Ali and Tipu defeated a British force. Students can see where the walls were breached in 1799 and where Tipu's body was found.

At Somanathapura, the star-shaped plan, lathe-turned pillars and signed sculpture panels make the Keshava Temple one of the best places to teach Hoysala architecture. The lecture on reading a temple prepares groups well, and Somanathapura is close in style to Belur and Halebidu, inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.

Museums in Mysuru

Jaganmohan Palace houses the Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery, with paintings by Raja Ravi Varma and traditional Mysore paintings. The Regional Museum of Natural History and the Folklore Museum at the University of Mysore (in Jayalakshmi Vilas) add other angles. The Daria Daulat Bagh at Srirangapatna has a small museum on Tipu's period. For a focused session, a museum gallery study with an archaeologist works in any of these.

Mysuru heritage walk for schools and colleges

For schools, a two-day plan works well: the palace and market on day one, Srirangapatna and Somanathapura by bus on day two. It covers the Anglo-Mysore wars, princely states and Hoysala art in one trip. Colleges in architecture and history can add the Hoysala sites further north.

We plan Mysuru walks with you, sized to your group and your time. The south India temple architecture study tour and a study tour built for your group can include Mysuru, Belur, Halebidu and Hampi.

Practical advice for groups

The palace is crowded on weekends and during Dasara (September or October), when it is lit up in the evenings. Photography rules inside the palace change, so check before you go. Srirangapatna's monuments are spread across the island; use a bus and walk between clusters. Check the ASI or site website for timings. For the wider state, see heritage sites in Karnataka.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Mysuru?

Mysore Palace, Jaganmohan Palace, the Devaraja Market, St Philomena's Church and Chamundi Hill in the city, with Srirangapatna (15 km) and the Keshava Temple at Somanathapura (about 35 km) as day trips.

When was Mysore Palace built?

The present palace was built between 1897 and 1912, designed by the British architect Henry Irwin, after the earlier wooden palace burned in 1897.

Is Somanathapura part of the UNESCO Hoysala listing?

Yes. The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, inscribed in 2023, include the temples at Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura.

How many days do school groups need in Mysuru?

Two days is comfortable: the palace and market on one, Srirangapatna and Somanathapura by bus on the other. One day is possible if you drop Somanathapura.
